sources.title: Toward Meta-cognitive Tutoring: A Model of Help Seeking with a Cognitive Tutor
sources.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
sources.verification: DOI + quote (abstract from openalex); minimax and mistral both "supported"
sources.quote: As a first test of the model’s efficacy, we used it off-line to evaluate students’ help-seeking behavior in an existing data set of student-tutor interactions.
sources.used_for: Help-seeking behaviour in an intelligent tutor, including ineffective help-seeking strategies, can be modelled and evaluated against logs of student-tutor interaction.

sources.title: Modeling and understanding students' off-task behavior in intelligent tutoring systems
sources.venue: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
sources.verification: DOI + quote (abstract from openalex); minimax and mistral both "supported"
sources.quote: We use this model in combination with motivational and attitudinal instruments, developing a profile of the attitudes and motivations associated with off-task behavior, and compare this profile to the attitudes and motivations associated with other behaviors in intelligent tutoring systems.
sources.used_for: Off-task behaviour of students in an intelligent tutoring system can be detected from system-usage logs, and it is associated with certain attitudes and motivations.

sources.title: Identifying emotional states using keystroke dynamics
sources.venue: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
sources.verification: DOI + quote (abstract from openalex); minimax and mistral both "supported"
sources.quote: Our solution is to determine user emotion by analyzing the rhythm of their typing patterns on a standard keyboard.
sources.used_for: A user's emotional state can be identified above chance from keystroke dynamics such as typing timing.

sources.title: Linguistic Style Matching in Social Interaction
sources.venue: Journal of Language and Social Psychology
sources.verification: DOI + quote (abstract from openalex); minimax and mistral both "supported"
sources.quote: The results of the three studies offer substantial evidence that individuals in dyadic interactions exhibit linguistic style matching (LSM) on both the conversation level as well as on a turn-by-turn level.
sources.used_for: People in conversation tend to match each other's linguistic style.

sources.title: Automatic personality assessment through social media language.
sources.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
sources.verification: DOI + quote (abstract from openalex); minimax and mistral both "supported"
sources.quote: Results indicated that language-based assessments can constitute valid personality measures: they agreed with self-reports and informant reports of personality, added incremental validity over informant reports, adequately discriminated between traits, exhibited patterns of correlations with external criteria similar to those found with self-reported personality, and were stable over 6-month intervals.
sources.used_for: Personality traits can be assessed automatically from the language of social media posts, with accuracy that correlates with self-reports.

sources.title: Large language models can infer psychological dispositions of social media users
sources.verification: DOI + quote (abstract from openalex); minimax and mistral both "supported"
sources.quote: Our results show an average correlation of r=0.29 (range=[0.22,0.33]) between LLM-inferred and self-reported trait scores—a level of accuracy that is similar to that of supervised machine learning models specifically trained to infer personality.
sources.used_for: Large language models can infer the Big Five personality traits of social media users from their posts, zero-shot, with modest correlations to self-reports.

sources.title: Predicting the proficiency level of language learners using lexical indices
sources.verification: DOI + quote (abstract from openalex); minimax and mistral both "supported"
sources.quote: In total, the indices correctly classified 70% of the texts based on proficiency level in both a training and a test set.
sources.used_for: Lexical indices computed from second-language learners' writing predict which proficiency level the learner belongs to.

sources.title: The Psychological Meaning of Words: LIWC and Computerized Text Analysis Methods
sources.venue: Journal of Language and Social Psychology
sources.verification: DOI + quote (abstract from openalex); minimax and mistral both "supported"
sources.quote: Empirical results using LIWC demonstrate its ability to detect meaning in a wide variety of experimental settings, including to show attentional focus, emotionality, social relationships, thinking styles, and individual differences.
sources.used_for: Counts of words in psychologically meaningful categories (LIWC) reveal attention, emotion, social relationships, thinking styles and individual differences.

sources.title: Personality in 100,000 Words: A large-scale analysis of personality and word use among bloggers
sources.verification: DOI + quote (abstract from semanticscholar); minimax and mistral both "supported"
sources.quote: The size of the dataset enabled pervasive correlations with personality to be identified for a broad range of lexical variables, including both aggregate word categories and individual English words.
sources.used_for: Personality traits correlate with the words people use in their blogs, in a large sample.

sources.title: Peeking at A/B Tests
sources.venue: ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD)
sources.verification: DOI + quote (abstract from openalex); minimax and mistral both "supported"
sources.quote: We provide always valid p-values and confidence intervals that are provably robust to this effect.
sources.used_for: Always-valid p-values and confidence intervals allow A/B test results to be monitored continuously with the error rate controlled, where repeatedly checking a fixed-sample test inflates false positives.
